_purpose: The ALIGNMENT GATE scene set. This is the check that clears all Indian training data, so it comes before any bulk pull.
_why_this_day: 2025-08-01 is peak monsoon AND we already hold one 3DR scan from it (2345Z). IMERG for the whole day is already downloaded and verified.
_why_these_times: Chosen from measured IMERG convection, not guessed. The gate needs a SHARP agreement peak, which comes from many separate heavy cores (cellular convection) rather than from a large rain area -- broad stratiform rain overlaps at any small offset and gives a flat, unidentifiable peak. That is exactly what happened on the 2345Z scene: peak/zero ratio 1.04x, below the 1.15x bar.
_scan_schedule: INSAT-3DR scans every 30 min at BOTH :15 and :45. The :15 slot is CONFIRMED by GPI files observed at that time. An earlier note called :15 unverified and removed it; that was over-cautious. Cadence for archive planning is 48 scans/day, not 24.

_imerg_pairing.2245: IMERG 2230-2259  152 heavy cores, score 151.8 (most cellular of the day)
_imerg_pairing.2345: IMERG 2330-2359  124 cores -- ALREADY HELD, measured but unidentifiable alone

_if_the_day_download_is_too_large: A full-disk scan is ~430 MB and a day is 48 of them (~20 GB) before the bbox is applied. If the bbox subset is still too large, the six times above are the ones that matter -- the rest can be discarded.
_CRITICAL: datasetId MUST be 3RIMG_L1B_STD (INSAT-3DR). A previous attempt returned a 3SIMG (INSAT-3DS) file instead, which is a different satellite at a different sub-satellite longitude (82E vs 74E) and therefore different parallax geometry.
